content:
Update, 11pm ET: Apple's System Status page shows all issues resolved. Original story below.

For the second time in a week, Apple is dealing with a major service outage affecting end users and developers. Here are the details.

According to Apple's System Status page, the following services are experiencing partial outages:

  • App Store: Some users affected. Users may be unable to make purchases in the iTunes Store, Mac App Store, and App Store.
  • AppleCare on Device: All users affected. AppleCare purchasing is temporarily unavailable.
  • iTunes Store: Some users affected. Users may be unable to make purchases in the iTunes Store, Mac App Store, and App Store.
  • Mac App Store: Some users affected. Users may be unable to make purchases in the iTunes Store, Mac App Store, and App Store.
  • Subscription Purchase: Some users affected. Users may experience intermittent issues with this service.

All issues began at 7:40pm ET and continue as of now. Additionally, Apple's Developer System Status page lists two ongoing issues that started at 7:20pm ET:

  • App Store – Advanced Commerce API: Some users affected. Affected services: App Store – Advanced Commerce API, App Store – In-App Purchases. We are currently performing emergency maintenance to improve system performance, with maintenance expected to take approximately two hours.
  • App Store – In-App Purchases: Some users affected. Affected services: App Store – Advanced Commerce API, App Store – In-App Purchases. We are currently performing emergency maintenance to improve system performance, with maintenance expected to take approximately two hours.

Although Apple says the emergency maintenance affecting developer services will take around two hours, it has not provided an estimated resolution time for the outage impacting users.

We'll update this article as more information becomes available.
